options.text: The wind blowing in the western ghats in winters is known as Loo.

questions.question: The violation of Fundamental Rights could be redressed by the Supreme Court under which of the following Articles?
questions.solution:

__
 
• ​We have legal recourse if any of** our rights are violated. **We can go straight to the **Supreme Court or the High Court of a state** if it involves a Fundamental Right. **The Right to Constitutional Remedies** was referred to by** Dr. Ambedkar** as the** "heart and soul" **of our **Constitution for this reason.**
 
• When a party's** fundamental rights are violated, **both the **Supreme Court and the high court have the authority to issue writs**. These writs include** mandamus, quo warranto, prohibition, habeas corpus, and certiorari.**
 
• **Article 32 is the heart and spirit of the Constitution,** according to **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, and rights granted by it will always be exercised in the** Supreme Court **unless an alteration has been made in it. 
 
• **Everybody, not just citizens, **have a right to access the **supreme court under Article 32 **of the constitution.

• **All of India's High Courts are authorised** to issue writs under **Article 226. **Writs of India are taken directly from "Prerogative writs" in English law.
 
• The Indian Constitution's** Article 265** addresses the issue of taxes that may only be levied by** legal permission.** It signifies that only legal authority has the** right to levy and collect taxes. **

questions.question: In physics, steradian is a unit of:

__

• The** term mass refers to the weight of a thing.** When you walk on a scale, for example, you are measuring the mass of your body. The gramme and kilogramme are the most frequent mass units in the metric system of measurement.
 
• Two straight lines intersecting at a location create a plane angle. The plane angle is the distance between these lines in the plane formed by them. It is measured in radians **(two radians in a circle) or degrees (360 degrees to a full circle).**
 
• **Length **can be measured in different units like** centimeters, inches, meters,** or by using a handspan, foot span, etc. The units of measuring length can be classified into two types: **Standard units of measuring length and non-standard units of measuring length.**

questions.question: The Vaishnava saint, Sankaradeva introduced the ______ dance in the 15th century CE.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Sattriya**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical Indian dance that originated in the eastern state of Assam. It was recognised as a classical dance by Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
 
• The modern form of Sattriya is **attributed to the 15th-century **Sankaradeva**,** who systematized the dance using the ancient texts, and introduced drama and expressive dancing** (nritta and nritya) **as a form of a community religious art for** emotional devotion to Krishna.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Manipuri Dance** also referred to as the** Manipuri Raas Leela,** is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of Manipur. The dance form is imbued with the devotional** themes of Madhura Raas of Radha-Krishna.**
 
• **Odissi,** also referred to as** Orissi in old literature**, is a major ancient Indian classical dance that originated in the temples of** Odisha – an eastern coastal state of India**
 
• **Kathak **is one of the **eight major forms of Indian classical danc**e. It is the classical dance form of** Uttar Pradesh. **The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards in ancient northern India known as** Kathakars or storytellers.**
